public class UserConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<User>
{
    public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<User> builder)

        builder.ToTable("Users");

        builder.HasKey(user => user.Id);

        builder.Property(user => user.Id)

        builder.Property(user => user.UserId)

            .IsRequired();

FlowForge is **well-suited for a small beta** — flat domain model, `AsNoTracking` on list reads, unique email index, scoped DbContext, and rate limiting are sensible foundations. title: Fix rate-limit test flakiness in ProjectCreateRateLimitTests and TaskCreateRateLimitTests
content:
⚠️ .NET TEST CONVENTIONS — MANDATORY: Use xUnit. All test classes must be `public sealed`. Use `[Fact]` and `[Theory]` attributes. Mock dependencies with NSubstitute or Moq. Never use `Thread.Sleep` — use `Task.Delay` with CancellationToken. Integration tests must use WebApplicationFactory<Program> with a separate test database — never the production database.

Always create fresh instances of services, repositories, and DbContext per test — never reuse a module-level singleton across tests. Use `beforeEach` (JS) or the xUnit constructor pattern (.NET) to initialise state. Cross-test state leakage causes flaky, order-dependent failures.

Update ProjectCreateRateLimitTests and TaskCreateRateLimitTests (in tests/FlowForge.Api.IntegrationTests/) to follow the established pattern: keep the main factory at PermitLimit=10000, introduce a separate low-limit factory only for the rate-limit assertions, and ensure no setup calls share the low-limit counter. Align with existing rate-limit test fixtures in the solution.

title: Result: Fix rate-limit test flakiness in ProjectCreateRateLimitTests and TaskCreateRateLimitTests
content:
## Coverage

Fixed rate-limit flakiness in `ProjectCreateRateLimitTests` and `TaskCreateRateLimitTests` by splitting setup from rate-limit assertions, matching the pattern described in the task and the test-executor note.

### Root cause

Both tests used a single factory with `PermitLimit=2` for all HTTP calls. Setup traffic (`POST /register`, and for tasks also `POST /projects`) consumed permits before the intended CRUD assertions ran, so the third create often returned 429 on the second attempt instead of the third.

### Fix

Introduced composite fixtures with **two factories sharing one SQLite in-memory connection**:

| Factory | PermitLimit | Used for |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| Setup | `10000` | Register, project create (task test only) |
| Rate-limit | `2` | Only the three create calls under test |

Rate limit counters are per app instance, so setup on the high-limit factory no longer affects the low-limit window. The shared DB keeps JWT auth valid across both clients.

### Files changed

**`tests/FlowForge.Tests/ProjectEndpointTests.cs`**
- `ProjectCreateRateLimitTestFixture` — owns shared connection + setup/rate-limit factories
- `ProjectCreateRateLimitTests` — register via `SetupClient`; project creates via `RateLimitClient`
- `ProjectCreateRateLimitWebApplicationFactory` — accepts shared connection + configurable `permitLimit`

**`tests/FlowForge.Tests/TaskEndpointTests.cs`**
- Same pattern for task create rate limiting
- Register + project create on `SetupClient`; task creates on `RateLimitClient`

Build succeeds with 0 warnings. Per author role, tests were not executed — test-executor should run:

dotnet test tests/FlowForge.Tests/FlowForge.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ProjectCreateRateLimitTests|FullyQualifiedName~TaskCreateRateLimitTests"
